self.disposition: orchestrator 7-point self-review; findings folded in (stale pr_review.py docstring; two of my own tests matched explanatory prose instead of parsed structure)

findings.finding: Privilege escalation via untrusted artifact execution. The spec states Stage 1 creates an artifact containing `JSON metadata + raw diff text` which Stage 2 reads and relies upon. If Stage 1 executes any repository code to gather this data (e.g., `git` hooks, `make` commands, custom scripts), a malicious fork PR can alter those scripts to generate a completely benign diff and falsify the metadata (e.g., `{ "sensitive_paths_touched": false }`). Stage 2 will then blindly approve the benign text and post a green status to the attacker's actual malicious head SHA.

Stage 2 cannot trust Stage 1’s tier/waiver decision, metadata, or even its diff when the PR is from the same repository. For same-repository PRs, a contributor can modify the Stage 1 workflow in their branch, causing it to upload a forged `meta.json`, an incomplete/benign diff, or a “waived” decision. Stage 2 correctly runs from the default branch, but that does not make the artifact trustworthy. This is especially material to AC10/E7: a PR changing `.github/workflows/` must not be able to declare itself exempt.
findings.suggestion: Make Stage 2 independently derive all authorization and policy inputs from trusted sources: resolve the PR from the trusted event/API, retrieve labels, author association, base/head SHA, and changed-file paths from the GitHub API, and apply the tier/waiver rules in Stage 2’s default-branch code. Prefer obtaining the reviewed diff directly from GitHub for the resolved PR/head SHA, or at minimum independently validate the artifact’s diff against a canonical API-derived diff. Treat artifact metadata as diagnostic only, never as an authority for PR identity, tier, waiver, changed paths, or review input.

findings.finding: The proposed least-privilege permission set may be insufficient for cross-run artifact retrieval. Downloading an artifact belonging to the triggering `workflow_run` commonly requires an Actions-artifact API call and therefore `actions: read`; setting explicit permissions makes unspecified permissions `none`. The stated Stage 2 scope of exactly `statuses: write`, `pull-requests: write`, and `contents: read` may cause artifact download to fail in production.
findings.suggestion: Confirm the exact artifact-download implementation against GitHub’s current permission requirements using the actual `actions/download-artifact` version and `run-id` mechanism. Add `actions: read` if required, and update AC12/the permission test to permit this narrowly justified read scope. Also verify the permission needed for the selected PR-comment API; depending on the client/API route, `issues: write` may be required rather than, or in addition to, `pull-requests: write`.

findings.finding: Resolving a fork PR solely from `workflow_run.head_sha` needs deterministic ambiguity handling. A head SHA can be associated with more than one PR in unusual but valid cases, including reused commits, multiple open PRs, or PR history states. Selecting the first API result could post a verdict/comment to the wrong PR. Force-push timing can also mean Stage 2 reviews an old SHA after the PR has advanced.
findings.suggestion: Query associated PRs by SHA and require exactly one eligible open PR in the expected base repository, with an exact head SHA match. If resolution is zero or ambiguous, fail closed and emit a clearly diagnosable workflow failure; do not choose arbitrarily and do not fall back to artifact PR metadata. For a superseded SHA, post only to that SHA if identity remains unambiguous; it will not satisfy the current head’s required context, which is the desired safe behavior.

findings.finding: Label-based waivers can remain green after the waiver is no longer valid unless label changes trigger a fresh Stage 1/Stage 2 evaluation on the same SHA. For example, if `skip-pr-review` produces a successful `PR Review` status and the label is later removed, a default `pull_request` trigger set (`opened`, `synchronize`, `reopened`) will not replace that success. The same concern applies if other tier inputs are label-driven.
findings.suggestion: Ensure Stage 1 explicitly triggers on `labeled` and `unlabeled` events for all policy-relevant labels, and that Stage 2 posts an updated status for the unchanged head SHA. On removal of a valid waiver, the refreshed result must be `pending`/failure until review completes, rather than leaving the prior successful waiver context in place. Add a behavioral test for waiver added then removed without a new push.

findings.finding: The artifact is attacker-controlled input and may cause resource exhaustion before the review code reaches its line-count or JSON-validation checks. An altered same-repo Stage 1 workflow can upload oversized artifacts; even fork artifacts can contain unexpectedly large diffs, malformed JSON, unusual filenames, or highly compressed content. `download-artifact` extraction occurs before a Python-level `--diff-file` size check.
findings.suggestion: Apply limits at both stages: enforce maximum diff byte size and line count before artifact upload in Stage 1, and enforce artifact/downloaded-file size limits in Stage 2 before parsing or invoking the reviewer. Download only the named artifact from the triggering run ID, require the expected file set (`pr.diff`, `meta.json`), reject unexpected paths/symlinks if the download mechanism exposes them, validate JSON against a bounded schema, and avoid logging raw artifact contents in failure messages.

findings.finding: “No stage-2 report means pending” is correctly fail-closed for merge protection, but several expected operational failures will be opaque: Stage 1 failure before upload, expired/missing artifact, artifact authorization failure, API rate-limit/error while resolving a PR, and status/comment API failure. The plan says messages must name the deliberate override for AC1–AC3, but a missing status gives maintainers no visible PR-level reason or recovery path.
findings.suggestion: After trusted PR resolution, make Stage 2 handle missing artifacts, malformed inputs, reviewer failures, and posting failures explicitly. Post a `failure` status with a concise reason whenever possible, and emit an actionable workflow summary describing the fallback (`skip-pr-review`, subject to the protected-path restriction) when the reviewer infrastructure is unavailable. Preserve “absent means blocked” only for failures that prevent even trusted identity resolution or status publication.

findings.finding: The rollback statement is slightly too broad: reverting this change restores the former workflow shape, but it also deliberately restores the known fork bypass and fail-open reviewer paths. That makes rollback an emergency availability action, not a safe functional rollback.
findings.suggestion: Document rollback as a security regression requiring an explicit operator decision, and include a safer operational fallback: temporarily leave the required `PR Review` context absent/blocking, use the constrained manual-waiver procedure, or restore only a corrected Stage 2 workflow.  Overall, the two-workflow design and moving the required context to a single Stage-2 commit-status producer are sound and address the skipped-check bypass directly. The main condition for this to be secure is that Stage 2 independently derives policy and review inputs from trusted GitHub state rather than treating the Stage-1 artifact as authoritative.

code.disposition: orchestrator-inline review of the full staged diff; no code-reviewer subagent (session constraint: Agent tool not authorised). Found+fixed: stale pr_review.py docstring naming a removed job; two tests asserting against their own explanatory prose; unused --diff-file flag reverted (YAGNI)

doubt.disposition: doubt-reviewer subagent not run (session constraint: Agent tool not authorised). Adversarial function served by two independent external reviewers, which found 5 real defects incl. 3 high-severity (artifact-supplied tier waiver, artifact-supplied diff, ambiguous PR resolution, force-push race, missing actions:read); all fixed and pinned by tests

findings.finding: The monorepo stage-2 workflow never writes a review verdict or reasons onto the PR. It only posts the `PR Review` commit status. This misses AC8, which requires both a PR comment containing the verdict/reasons and a status on the head SHA. It also means waived internal PRs have no visible record explaining why the required context was marked successful.
findings.suggestion: Add a PR-comment step, after trusted PR resolution, that posts the tier reason for waived PRs and the reviewer output/verdict for reviewed PRs. Make the success status depend on that comment succeeding when a comment is required.

findings.finding: PR resolution arbitrarily selects the first open PR associated with the event SHA (`[0].number`). A commit SHA can legitimately be associated with multiple open PRs, potentially with different base branches and diffs. The workflow can therefore review/comment on one PR’s current diff but post a successful `PR Review` status to the shared SHA, satisfying the gate for another PR that was not the reviewed change.
findings.suggestion: Fetch all associated PRs and require exactly one eligible open PR targeting `main` whose `.head.sha` exactly equals `HEAD_SHA`; fail closed on zero or multiple matches. Before review and status publication, also verify the selected PR’s current head SHA still equals the event SHA.

findings.finding: The review input is fetched using the mutable PR number (`gh pr diff` inside `pr_review.py`), but the verdict is posted to the immutable `workflow_run.head_sha`. If the PR is force-pushed after stage 1 completes, stage 2 may review the new head while marking the old SHA successful. If that old SHA is later restored, it can inherit a green status based on a review of different content. This also does not meet the stated requirement that the reviewed diff be derived at the trusted head SHA.
findings.suggestion: After resolving the PR, query and require `.head.sha == HEAD_SHA`, and obtain/review a diff explicitly pinned to that validated SHA/base pair. Fail rather than review if the PR has advanced.

findings.finding: AC4 requires each of the oversize, reviewer-crash, and unparseable-output failures to name the deliberate override in its actionable failure message. The oversize branch does this, but a non-zero `claude` exit relies on `set -e` and produces no workflow-authored actionable message or override guidance. The JSON-parse failure explains fail-closed behavior but likewise does not name the deliberate override.
findings.suggestion: Wrap the reviewer command in a failure handler that emits an explicit `::error::` explaining that the reviewer failed and identifying the approved deliberate override. Add the same override guidance to the parse-failure message while preserving a non-zero failure.

findings.finding: The workflow reacts to `labeled` but not `unlabeled`. A PR can receive `skip-pr-review`, get a successful waiver status without a review, then have the label removed without a push. The already-green `PR Review` status remains on that SHA and no replacement stage-2 evaluation occurs, so removal does not actually revoke the waiver.
findings.suggestion: Add `unlabeled` to the `pull_request.types` trigger and ensure the resulting stage-2 run replaces the status with a review result/failure for the unchanged SHA. Consider posting a pending/failure status as early as possible when revoking a waiver to minimize the interval in which the stale success remains usable.

findings.finding: The tests described as pinning AC1–AC3 do not actually validate those behaviors. `test_oversize_diff_fails_instead_of_skipping` only searches for any `exit 1` anywhere in the workflow, not that it is reachable from the size threshold; changing the threshold comparison to the wrong direction would pass. `test_unparseable_review_output_fails_closed` only rejects the old “skipping comment” text, so a catch block that silently returns under different wording would pass. There is also no test asserting an explicit reviewer-error handler/actionable override message required by AC4.
findings.suggestion: Parse the relevant step bodies and assert the size comparison branches to a non-zero exit, the reviewer command’s non-zero result reaches a failing path, and parse errors invoke `core.setFailed`/throw rather than return successfully. Add assertions for the deliberate-override text on all three failure paths.  Overall assessment: block until the missing monorepo PR comment and unsafe SHA-to-PR/diff binding are fixed. The two-stage architecture is directionally correct and mostly fail-closed, but these defects leave required acceptance criteria unimplemented and permit verdicts to be associated with the wrong change in valid PR/SHA states.
